errors.english: Here too, the ritual procedure is not like that of the calming ritual.
errors.why: The Tibetan says the procedure here is the same as for pacifying; the negation is added.

fix.find: Here too, the ritual procedure is not like that of the calming ritual.
fix.replace: Here too, the ritual procedure is the same as that of the calming ritual.

errors.english: residing within the great elemental (mandala)
errors.why: dbang chen gyi dkyil 'khor is the Mahendra (earth) maṇḍala, not a 'great elemental' maṇḍala.

note: Generally faithful ritual commentary; one negation inverted that reverses the instruction for the increasing rite.

errors.english: this shows his primary qualities
errors.why: The Tibetan says this teaches the non-principal (secondary) sense, not the primary one.

fix.replace: this teaches the secondary sense [of the word]

errors.english: Page 28
errors.why: The Tibetan has nothing corresponding; 'Page 28' is extraneous text.

errors.english: because the letter 'a' [note: referring to a Sanskrit grammatical rule] possessing the meaning of the root is elided
errors.why: ma'i don refers to the possessive suffix (matup), whose sense the elided 'a' carries, not 'the root'.

note: Sound rendering of a grammatical etymology of 'buddha' and the opening of the Dharmānusmṛti commentary, with one inverted negation.

errors.english: These details regarding gender and markers were not present in the earlier translations [note: the Old Translation period] of the Indic manuscripts.
errors.why: Reading sdang as snang, the note says these (gender etc.) appear in the earlier translation but are absent from the Indic manuscript.

errors.english: according to the "logic of the staff and the load"
errors.why: khur ba here is 'cake': this is the daṇḍāpūpa-nyāya (maxim of the stick and the cakes), not 'staff and load'.

note: Amarakośa commentary with heavy Sanskrit; transliterations are rough and the grammatical argument is only partly secured.

errors.english: Born from karma [note: the original implies action or cause], it is the growth of the head, which is the hair.
errors.why: las is the ablative completing mgo (previous side): 'because it is born from the head it is head-born, i.e. hair'; nothing about karma.

note: Faithful epithet-by-epithet commentary; only the opening ablative misread as 'karma'.

errors.english: In common usage regarding items like clothing, the status of something as a cause is observed through direct perception and the observation of its absence
errors.why: The Tibetan says that, apart from the well-known causes of cloth etc., [adṛṣṭa] is NOT ascertained as a cause by perception and non-perception or by absence of effect; the English presents the ascertainment as observed and drops 'apart from its well-known causes'.

errors.english: a produced thing or other items such as a staff would also become the cause of birth
errors.why: In this Vaiśeṣika guṇa context 'dus byas pa renders saṃskāra (the quality 'impetus/disposition'), not a 'produced thing'; same in the next sentence.

errors.english: The "unseen agent" [note: referring to the concept of Adrishta or unseen karmic potential] is the giver of the result.
errors.why: The unseen (adṛṣṭa) is what gives the agent his result; it is not an 'unseen agent'.

note: Argument broadly followed, but the opening point about how causality is ascertained is blurred and saṃskāra is mistranslated.

errors.english: and cow urine
errors.why: chāgamūtra is goat's urine; the note's 'likely bovine' is also wrong.

errors.english: allow the materials to float
errors.why: What floats in the half-filled copper vessel is the gold or silver pot holding the substances (previous side), not the loose materials.

note: Careful rendering of the perfumery procedures with one wrong ingredient.

errors.english: I, the preceptor named [note: insert preceptor name here], shall now question this candidate named [note: insert candidate name here] regarding the obstructive conditions.
errors.why: The speaker is the officiating monk; 'whose preceptor is N.' describes the candidate, so the preceptor is not the one who questions.

fix.find: I, the preceptor named [note: insert preceptor name here], shall now question this candidate named [note: insert candidate name here] regarding the obstructive conditions.
fix.replace: I shall now question this candidate named [note: insert candidate name here], whose preceptor is [note: insert preceptor name here], regarding the obstructive conditions.

errors.english: Are you not a runaway?
errors.why: brkus pa means stolen/abducted, not a runaway.

note: Clear rendering of the bhikṣuṇī ordination formulary, but the motion misattributes who does the questioning.

errors.english: "This form is mine,"
errors.why: The Tibetan says 'this form is the self' (bdag), not 'mine' (bdag gi).

note: Faithful Prajñāpāramitā commentary with one misidentified view of self.

errors.english: [note: This indicates the patience of subsequent realization regarding cessation.]
errors.why: This sentence is the commentator's own gloss in the Tibetan text, not a translator's note.

note: Accurate rendering of the repetitive interrogation through the links of dependent origination.

errors.english: the nature of concealed truth and relative truth
errors.why: The pair is relative (saṃvṛti) and ultimate (paramārtha) truth; the English gives two names for the relative.

fix.find: the nature of concealed truth and relative truth
fix.replace: the nature of relative truth and ultimate truth

errors.english: the dharmakāya, sambhogakāya, and nirmāṇakāya
errors.why: The Tibetan names only the dharmakāya and sambhogakāya.

errors.english: This interpretation, which has been passed down through a lineage of transmission, is favored by some.
errors.why: The Tibetan says this is the explanation according to the authentic transmission; 'favored by some' is not there.

note: Polished and largely faithful Hevajra commentary; a few points diverge from the Tibetan, notably the two truths.
